name: it_sector_correlation_arb_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: TCS and INFY have a 0.90+ correlation on daily returns, but intraday correlation drops to 0.70-0.80 due to asynchronous order flow. When the intraday spread between TCS and INFY (log-price ratio) deviates by > 1.5 SD from its intraday mean, it reverts within 30-60 bars. This is specifically an IT sector play: both stocks are driven by the same macro factors (USD/INR, US tech sentiment, IT spending) but different institutional allocations create temporary divergences. Edge persists because the pair is liquid enough to trade but spread monitoring requires automation.

long.confirmation: long TCS, short INFY; enter when zscore starts reverting

short.confirmation: short TCS, long INFY; enter when zscore starts reverting

exit.stop_loss: log_ratio_zscore reaches ±2.5 or 0.4% absolute loss on combined position
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven when zscore crosses ±0.5

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: both TCS and INFY must have volume > 50% of their 20-bar avg
filters.spread_filter: skip if either stock has spread > 0.06%
filters.event_filter: skip on result day for either stock; skip if USDINR moves > 0.5% intraday

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — well-known pair but intraday spread is less competed

weaknesses: Two-leg execution doubles all costs — need > 25 bps gross spread to profit after costs
TCS/INFY correlation can break during result season or sector-specific news (e.g., one wins a mega deal)
Log ratio z-score with 120-bar lookback is unstable in the first hour of trading
prior_art: TCS/INFY pairs trade — one of the most classic Indian market pair trades
notes: Can extend to include WIPRO, HCLTECH for a multi-name IT sector spread.
